body.heading: Small beats grand
paragraphs: Families imagine rituals as big productions: the perfect holiday table, the annual trip planned for months. But the rituals people still remember at forty are usually tiny — pancakes on Saturdays, a song in the car, the exact way goodnight was always said.
A ritual sticks when it is easy enough to survive a busy week. If it needs planning, booking, or good weather, it will quietly die by February.

body.heading: Start one this week
paragraphs: Pick something that takes under fifteen minutes and attaches to a moment that already exists: one question at dinner, a short walk after Sunday lunch, a shared dessert on Fridays.
Let it be imperfect, and let everyone shape it. The rituals that last are the ones the whole family feels they own — including the silly parts nobody planned.

description: The rituals families keep for decades are rarely the elaborate ones — they are small, easy, and a little bit silly.
